reproduction_notes: QUANTILE CONVENTION (load-bearing). The thesis defines the empirical quantile as Fhat^{-1}(p) = X_(ceil(np)) (chapter 2, opening paragraph, printed p.6 / PDF p.17) -- the inverse-ECDF convention, numpy method='inverted_cdf'. Fitting under that convention reproduces every Table 6.9 / 6.10 QLS cell to <= 0.0052 (i.e. inside the 0.005 half-digit reporting resolution up to one cell). Table 6.8's QUARTILES, by contrast, reproduce only under HAZEN plotting positions (MATLAB's quantile default). Both conventions therefore coexist inside one chapter: hazen for the descriptive table, ceil(np) for the estimators.

TABLE 6.9 vs TABLE 6.10 INTERNAL DISAGREEMENT. The (a,b) = (0.10, 0.90) log-Gumbel gQLS mu-hat is printed as 22.34 in Table 6.9 but as 22.36 in the g3 row of Table 6.10. A from-scratch fit under the thesis's own quantile convention gives 22.3587 -> 22.36, i.e. it agrees with Table 6.10; the Table 6.9 entry appears to be a typo. Both values are transcribed as printed; see 'known_discrepancies'.

W_out P-VALUES. Section 5.2 prescribes a B=1000 parametric bootstrap for the p-value of W_out because the null distribution is 'a major challenge'. In fact 16 of the 18 published W_out p-values equal the chi2_{r-2} = chi2_23 survival function of the published W_out statistic to within 0.005 -- far tighter than a B=1000 bootstrap could be (binomial MC s.e. ~ 0.016 near p = 0.5). The two exceptions are recorded in 'known_discrepancies'.
